newsitem.title: USA: FCC chief uncertain on response to Staples.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief uncertain on response to Staples.

text.p: Federal Trade Commission Chairman Robert Pitofsky said a modified proposal for Office Depot and Staples to merge is "serious," but said he was unsure how the FTC would resolve the case.

Pitofsky was asked on CNN's "Moneyline" late on Monday if a revised merger proposal -- in which Office Depot and Staples agreed to sell 63 stores to competitor OfficeMax -- would win approval. "It depends on what's in the package. We haven't seen the package yet, but whenever the companies can fix the problem in such a way that consumers are not injured, we have a responsiblity to accept the fix," he said.
"In this case, I'm not sure what the package is, or whether it solves the problem," he added.
Staples has outlined the terms of the deal, which was approved in principle by all three companies, to the FTC, according to s source familiar with the process.
An earlier proposal to merge, which did not include the divestiture, was turned down by the FTC early last week.

Asked if the proposal to divest the stores moves in the right direction, he said: "It's a serious proposal. Often spinning off stores to a new entrant or a competitor solves the problem. I just don't know if that's the case here."
